what_its_for: Mafenide is an antibiotic cream or solution used to help prevent and treat bacterial infections in burn wounds. It is applied directly to the skin to keep germs from growing in the burned area and to help the wound heal.
how_to_take: Mafenide is applied directly to your burn wound on the skin — it is NOT taken by mouth. Wash your hands thoroughly before and after applying this medicine. Clean the burn area as directed by your healthcare team. Using a clean gloved hand or sterile applicator, apply a thin layer (about 1/16 inch thick) of the cream to the entire burn surface. Keep the burn area covered with the cream at all times. Your nurse or doctor will show you exactly how to apply it.
dosing: Cream: Apply once or twice daily (every 12 to 24 hours) to cover the burn wound completely. Solution (dressing): Your wound dressing should be kept moist with the solution every 4 hours, or as directed by your doctor. Always follow the specific instructions given by your healthcare provider, as dosing depends on the size and depth of your burn.
missed_dose: If you miss an application, apply the cream or re-wet the dressing as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next scheduled application, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not apply extra amounts to make up for a missed dose. Contact your care team if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store mafenide cream at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and freezing temperatures. Keep the container tightly closed when not in use. Store out of reach of children. Do not use the product after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting mafenide in your eyes, nose, mouth, or ears. Do not swallow this medicine. Avoid applying other creams, ointments, or lotions to the burn area unless your doctor tells you to. Do not use tight bandages or dressings that trap air unless instructed by your care team. Tell your doctor if you are taking sulfa-type antibiotics by mouth, as mafenide is also a sulfa drug and combining them may increase side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: difficulty breathing or rapid breathing, which may be a sign of a serious reaction; signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or dizziness; signs of a blood disorder such as unusual fatigue, pale skin, or shortness of breath; confusion or unusual drowsiness; pain or burning that gets much worse after applying the cream; signs of a worsening infection such as increased redness, warmth, swelling, pus, or a bad smell from the wound; or skin rash or itching that spreads beyond the wound area.
when_it_works: Mafenide starts working to fight bacteria in your wound right away after it is applied. However, burn wound healing is a slow process that can take days to weeks or even longer depending on how serious your burn is. You may not notice visible improvement for several days. Keep using it exactly as directed even if you do not see immediate changes.
special_populations: Children: Mafenide can be used in children but must be used with great caution and under close medical supervision, as children may be more sensitive to side effects. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of mafenide during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Kidney or lung disease: Use with extra caution if you have kidney problems, lung problems, or acid-base imbalances in your blood, as mafenide can affect your body's acid-base balance. Sulfa allergy: Tell your doctor if you have ever had an allergic reaction to sulfa drugs, as mafenide belongs to the same drug family.
